sections.h2: Where is Braintree and how big is it?
sections.html:
Braintree is a community of 39,143 residents (2020 census) in Norfolk County, south of Boston on the South Shore. It covers about 14.6 square miles, and only 0.8 of those are water.

Quincy borders Braintree on the north, Weymouth on the east and Holbrook on the south. Randolph lies to the west, separated from Braintree by the Cochato River. Parks and open space include Pond Meadow Park, Sunset Lake and part of the Blue Hills Reservation, and South Shore Plaza is the best known retail destination in town.

Braintree has two historic village centers, Braintree and South Braintree, which were separate communities in 1888. The ZIP codes are 02184 and 02185.

sections.h2: Is Braintree a town or a city?
sections.html:
Braintree is officially the Town of Braintree, yet it has been a city under Massachusetts law since 2007, with a mayor and a town council. The first mayor was Joe Sullivan, who served until January 2020. Erin Joyce was elected mayor in 2023.

That naming matters when you look for paperwork. Departments such as the Assessors, the Collector and the Treasurer sit under Municipal Finance on the official website, braintreema.gov.

sections.h2: What is the history of Braintree?
sections.html:
Settlers arrived in 1625 on land first called Mount Wollaston, and the town was incorporated in 1640. Its original territory later split into Quincy in 1792 and Randolph in 1793, and Holbrook broke off Randolph in 1872. Braintree was part of Suffolk County until Norfolk County was formed in 1793.

John Adams and John Hancock are both on the list of notable people from Braintree. In 1920 it was the site of the murders that led to the Sacco and Vanzetti trial. Its population grew by more than half that same decade, and after World War II some Irish American and Italian American families moved to Braintree from lower income parts of Boston.

The 2020 census counted 39,143 residents, and Wikipedia's 2024 estimate is 39,134, so the population has been flat since then.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers and schools in Braintree?
sections.html:
Large companies listed for the town include Altra Industrial Motion, Greater Media and TopSource LLC.

Braintree Public Schools run six elementary schools (Flaherty, Highlands, Hollis, Liberty, Morrison and Ross), two middle schools (East and South) and Braintree High School. A kindergarten center was closed in 2024. Private options in town include Thayer Academy, Archbishop Williams High School and CATS Academy Boston.

For sellers, school attendance zones are set by the district, so ask the school office which elementary school serves your street instead of relying on a listing site.

sections.h2: How does Braintree connect to Boston and the Cape?
sections.html:
Braintree has several rail options. Braintree station is served by the MBTA Red Line, two commuter rail lines (the Fall River/New Bedford Line and the Kingston Line) and the seasonal CapeFLYER. The Weymouth Landing/East Braintree station on the Weymouth border is served by the Greenbush Line.

RouteWhat it does in Braintree
I-93 and US 1Come in from Boston on the Southeast Expressway, then head west toward Route 128
Route 3Splits south toward Cape Cod as the Pilgrims Highway
Routes 37 and 53Other principal highways in town
Red LineRapid transit from Braintree station

Braintree once had its own airport near Great Pond, open from 1948 to 1968. It closed because of residential development, nearby water supply concerns and a number of accidents.

sections.h2: How do weather and water affect a Braintree house?
sections.html:
Braintree has a humid continental climate with some ocean influence, and it averages about 48.6 inches of precipitation and about 61 inches of snow in a season. Snow totals swing widely. The winter of 2011 to 2012 brought 24.2 inches, and the winter of 2014 to 2015 brought 150.8 inches.

  • Nor'easters are the main storm threat, and the last tropical system to affect the city was Hurricane Sandy in October 2012.
  • Thunderstorms from May to September can bring large hail and damaging winds.
  • Braintree has never been struck by a violent tornado, though it has had many tornado warnings.

Water service is a local topic too. In 2020 Braintree, Randolph and Holbrook formed the Tri-Town Water Board, and Braintree runs its own water treatment plant. That is background for a seller rather than a sale requirement.

sections.h2: What are Braintree's tax rates for fiscal 2026?
sections.html:
The Braintree Assessors publish the fiscal 2026 rates per $1,000 of assessed value:

ClassRate per $1,000
Residential$10.06
Commercial and industrial$21.39
Personal property$21.33

At $10.06, a house assessed at $650,000 carries about $6,539 in annual tax before exemptions. Treat that as arithmetic, not a bill.

The Assessors' office is at 1 John F. Kennedy Memorial Drive, and the phone is 781-794-8050. It helps owners with exemption forms, abatement forms and abutter lists, and it runs a property record website. Town Hall is open Monday, Wednesday and Thursday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Tuesday until 7 p.m., and Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m.

An abatement application must be filed on or before the due date of the first actual tax bill, and the Appellate Tax Board guide says that is generally February 1 where bills are quarterly. Confirm your schedule on your bill.

sections.h2: What happens if a Braintree owner appeals an assessment?
sections.html:
An owner who disagrees with the Braintree Assessors files an abatement application first, and assessors then have three months to act on it. If they deny it or do nothing, the owner has three months to appeal to the Appellate Tax Board.

  • The tax bill must be paid on time for the board to hear the case, with limited exceptions.
  • Hearings are held at the board's office in Boston or by video, and most single family hearings last one to two hours.
  • A case usually takes four months to a year to reach a hearing.
  • The owner has to show the home's fair cash value is below its assessed value, and comparable sales help.

If you are selling soon, the appeal may not finish before closing, so ask your attorney how any refund is handled.

sections.h2: What does a deed cost to record in Norfolk County?
sections.html:
Braintree is in Norfolk County, and the Norfolk County Registry of Deeds charges $2.28 in excise tax for each $500 of the sale price or fraction of it, collected when the deed is recorded.

Sale priceExcise at $2.28 per $500
$155,000 (registry's own example)$706.80
$500,000$2,280
$650,000$2,964
  • The registry lists a $156 fee to record a deed in recorded land and $155 in registered land.
  • The excise tax needs its own attorney's check or bank check, separate from the recording fee.
  • A municipal lien certificate has an $81 recording fee at the registry.
  • Documents filed electronically avoid the $1 postage charge as of July 1, 2025.

sections.h2: What should a Braintree seller finish before closing?
sections.html:
You need a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate of compliance from the Braintree fire department for the sale of a home. Call once you have a closing date, and expect a fee. Alarms that are past their date or lack a date must be replaced.

Massachusetts treats real estate closings as work for an attorney, and about 80 to 90 percent of properties are recorded land filed at the registry. A home inspection can be part of the deal, and state rules prevent a seller from requiring a buyer to waive it on certain residential sales.

If the house has a septic system, Title 5 calls for an inspection within two years before the sale. Check whether your property has one.

sections.h2: What do Braintree sellers usually face?
sections.html: The town grew from 10,580 people in 1920 to 35,050 in 1970, so much of Braintree was built up during those decades. When an older family home passes to heirs who live elsewhere, a direct sale avoids showings and staging. We buy Braintree houses as they are.

faqs.q: Is Braintree a city or a town?
faqs.a: Both. Its official name is the Town of Braintree, but it has had a mayor and council government since 2007 and counts as a city under Massachusetts law.

faqs.q: What is the residential tax rate in Braintree?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2026 the Braintree Assessors list $10.06 per $1,000 of assessed value for residential property.

faqs.q: What is the deed excise tax in Norfolk County?
faqs.a: The Norfolk County Registry of Deeds charges $2.28 for each $500 of the sale price or fraction of it. A $500,000 sale comes to $2,280.
Braintree station has the Red Line, the Fall River/New Bedford and Kingston commuter rail lines, and seasonal CapeFLYER service. The Greenbush Line stops at Weymouth Landing/East Braintree.

faqs.q: Do I need a fire department certificate to sell a house in Braintree?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing that smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the rules for a sale.
